title: Halo prefetch vs tiling: economics and latency sampler
content:
Purpose:
Quick, experiment-forward writeup comparing a lightweight 'halo prefetch' policy (predictive short-range prefix prefetching) against the existing tiling/slotization flow. Goal: quantify p50/p95/p99 latency impact and dollars-per-1k-requests for a mixed chat+completion workload with microbursts.

Motivation / context (notes to self):
- We need an approach between full predictive prefetch and pure tiling to reduce microburst p95 without blowing up token cost.
- Halo prefetch = prefetch up to N tokens ahead for requests likely to continue (simple classifier + short horizon).
- Tiling = pack multiple sessions into a tile/slot to amortize kernel startup. Works great for sustained concurrency but suffers on short-lived microbursts (start-up penalty).
- This doc is experimental: numbers are from a 3-run median on dev cluster (2xA100, smallish infra). Not production SLA.

Experiment design:
- Model: open-llama-13B-8k (fp16, baseline), and quantized 4-bit variant (int4-fast).
- HW: 2xA100 (40GB) per node, 256MB KV working set during bursts
- Traffic mix: 65% chat-like (turns, avg tokens per turn 35), 35% completion (avg tokens 120)
- Burst profile: steady background 60 rps, random 2s microbursts to 800 rps, ~10 bursts per minute
- Policies tested:
  1) baseline-tiling: slot_size=16, opportunistic packing, no prefetch
  2) halo-prefetch: classifier threshold 0.6, horizon=8 tokens, KV hints enabled, slot_size=8
  3) hybrid: halo-prefetch + tiling slot_size=12
- Metric capture: p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), tokens-per-second throughput, cost-est (dollars per 1k requests, simplified using per-GPU-minute cost and amortized token cost).

Raw (aggregated medians across 3 runs) -- text table:

Policy | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | TPU equiv throughput (tps) | cost per 1k reqs (USD)
-------|---------|---------|---------|---------------------------|-----------------------
baseline-tiling | 38 | 420 | 980 | 125 | 5.40
halo-prefetch  | 44 | 210 | 360 | 138 | 6.20
hybrid         | 40 | 195 | 320 | 140 | 6.05

Observations / quick interpretation:
- Baseline tiling gives better p50 and slightly lower measured cost, but p95/p99 are large during microbursts (980ms p99). That indicates cold-start/slotization effects at the tail.
- Halo-prefetch reduces tail latency substantially (p99 reduced ~63%), at expense of raising median slightly and increasing token cost ~15% (prefetched tokens consumed or wasted).
- Hybrid mixes benefits: nearly baseline median, tail close to halo, cost in between. Suggests partial tiling + short horizon prefetch is a strong candidate for bursty workloads.

ASCII chart: p99 latency across timeline (sample run, 1 minute slice, values in ms)
Time(s)    0   5  10  15 20  25 30 35 40 45 50 55 60
baseline    120 150 200 420 650 980 720 430 310 260 240 230 220
halo        90 100 130 210 260 360 250 190 160 150 145 143 140
hybrid      95 110 140 195 230 320 260 200 170 160 155 152 150

Cost breakdown (notes):
- Cost here modeled as GPU-minutes * infra-rate + token-waste penalty (prefetched but unused).
- Baseline-tiling achieved slightly lower GPU utilization variance (fewer small in-flight kernels), leading to lower apparent cost. But under higher infra price assumptions (reserved capacity model), tail penalties can cause SLA credits which flip economics.

Micro-profile: where halo helps most
- Short sessions where user types 1-2 tokens then continues after ~200ms: tiling often misses because it waits for pack threshold; halo prefetch ensures KV warm and small decode kernel primed.
- Long completions: prefetch horizon is irrelevant, tiling amortizes decode cost better.

Failure modes and caveats:
- Prefetch classifier false positives -> wasted tokens. We measured false-positive rate ~12% at threshold=0.6; that maps to ~7% extra token cost overall. Tune threshold or use per-tenant priors.
- Prefetch increases concurrency at decode stage; must watch slot contention and memory fragmentation. Additional GC churn observed in one run (spikes in allocation).
- Experiments run on 2xA100 dev nodes; results will differ on Hopper / L40x or in dedicated multi-tenant fleet.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Run same suite on 4xH100 (or L4x) to compare kernel startup differences (H100 startup is cheaper, may reduce p99 gap).
- Add a 'cost with SLA credits' simulation: assume p95 SLA 500ms, model penalty schedule and re-evaluate net economics across policies.
- Try classifier improvements: lightweight RNN (O(100)ns) vs heuristics (presence of continuation tokens) to cut false positives.
- Produce a compact one-pager for sales showing: median vs p99 tradeoff and recommended hybrid config for bursty webchat.

Actionable configuration suggestions (proto):
- Default dev/higher-priority customers: hybrid with halo horizon=8, tiling slot_size=12, classifier threshold=0.65.
- Low-cost tier (best-effort): baseline-tiling slot_size=16, no prefetch.

Notes / links / stray references:
- See jira JIRA-ENG-3421 for the classifier training dataset and CLI to replay bursts.
- Slack thread: #runtime-burst (link pinned) — Evan posted traces on 2026-02-18.
- Related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/tiling-proto/pull/88 (hybrid orchestration sketch).

Open questions (for review):
- How much do clients object to increased median p50 for slightly better tail? UX product asks for median-first for interactive editors. We need product's tolerance band.
- Do we want per-tenant adaptive thresholds? That adds complexity to control plane.

Sign-off draft (for internal review):
